 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Joao Gomes should be handed a start in Aston Villa's clash with Sunderland. 
 Unai Emery's side host the Black Cats at Villa Park on Saturday, as they return from the international break.
 The former Wolves midfielder has started 10 times in his 13 appearances for the Villans so far, since his summer move.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 25-year-old must be handed the responsibility again over German midfielder Leon Goretzka.
 The former Bayern Munich ace got the nod in the draws with  Fulham  and Man United, and that must change.
 How did Joao Gomes perform last time out for Aston Villa? 
 Ex-Wolves boss Rob Edwards labelled Gomes as a "wonderful player" in March after a win against Villa, and his talent was evident against Fulham.
 The Rio de Janeiro-born ace only played 24 minutes against the Cottagers, but he had an impact regardless.
 The Brazilian made three passes into the final third and three line-breaking passes in the contest, per FotMob data.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Defensively, he made two contributions in his limited time on the pitch, with one tackle and one recovery.
 The only aspect of his cameo that let him down was the fact that he won just one of three ground duels, for a 33 per cent success rate.
 Aston Villa predicted XI vs Sunderland: Matty Cash alternative named, Leon Goretzka axed How did Goretzka perform in Villa's draw with Fulham? 
 Goretzka did not do much better than Gomes in the last draw at home, in his 66 minutes on the field.
 The experienced star recorded three passes into the final third and five line-breaking passes.
 The 31-year-old made four defensive contributions, with one tackle, one clearance and two recoveries.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In terms of duels, he won 50 per cent of his four on the ground and 33 per cent of three in the air against Alvaro Arbeloa's side.
 Those figures are only slightly better that Gomes' numbers, so it is not unreasonable to suggest that the younger man would do better with more time on the pitch.
